title: Grove's Pioneer Chain incentives target Avalanche but the incentive pool sits on Ethereum Mainnet in Grove's SubProxy
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.5.3.2.1 configures the Avalanche Instance of the Pioneer Chain Primitive. Its Instance identifier network (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.3.2.1.1.1) is `Avalanche`, but the Pioneer Incentive Pool beneath it declares its own network (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.3.2.1.1.2.1) as `Ethereum Mainnet`, with an address (A.6.1.1.2.2.5.3.2.1.1.2.2) of `0x1369f7b2b38c76B6478c0f0E66D94923421891Ba`.

That address is Grove's **SubProxy Account**, given in A.6.1.1.2.2.1.1.3.1.1.2. So the "Pioneer Incentive Pool" is not a dedicated contract or a segregated vault — it is the Agent's general onchain account, designated for this purpose by the Artifact rather than by any onchain separation.

Two consequences follow. First, the incentive program for one chain is funded and controlled from another, which is coherent for a Sky Agent whose governance and treasury live on Ethereum, but means Avalanche-side participants depend on Ethereum-side execution. Second, because the pool shares an address with Grove's other holdings — including the other Agents' tokens it must custody there per A.6.1.1.2.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.1 — the pool's balance cannot be read directly from chain state. It is defined by the Artifact and the terms it references (A.2.2.9.3.1.4), not by a segregated balance.

The pattern to note is that the Atlas frequently establishes economic separation **by document** where a reader might assume separation by contract. Verifying such a pool requires reading the terms, not querying an address.
description: The Avalanche Instance's Pioneer Incentive Pool address is the same SubProxy account that holds Grove's other assets — the pool is an accounting designation, not a segregated wallet.
